label: input r in the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter r during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and only near the start of the sequence. Magnitude decays steadily with position: about 1.0 x max at t=0, about 0.75-0.87 at t=1, about 0.43-0.57 at t=2, and weak (0.03-0.2) at t=3. It never fires at t>=4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, including when r is fed back as a copy input. It also never fires on any other token. A repeated r (e.g. r r at t=0,1) still fires, so this is not a first-occurrence detector. The predicate t<=2 has precision 1.0 and drops only the weak t=3 tail; dev F1 0.955, mass recall 0.99.

issues: No refuting evidence found. Test scores match exactly: P 1.000, R 0.915, F1 0.956, mass recall 0.993.

'Never fires in delimiter/copy phase' holds: phase != 0 gives 0 active out of 3.23M predicted steps (test). The dev profile shows 0 active at the delimiter and in the copy phase, even though r is input there.
'Never fires on another token' holds: in_tok != r gives precision 0 over 6.27M steps.
Repeated r still fires: the t<=2 subset with r already seen has precision 1.0 (n=1598).

The t=3 tail is weak and only partial. r at t=3 fires about 29% of the time (precision 0.286), at 0.02-0.19 x max, and holds 0.7% of mass. prev_tok being a digit does not explain it (P 0.33). There are 0 false positives and no systematic pattern remains.
Minor wording: the profile splits mass across t=0/1/2 as 0.43/0.35/0.21, which fits the stated decay. The label is accurate.
